Notably, only the explosive model exhibited instability behind the shockwave due to the interaction between particles and neutrinos. This could be attributed to the density of the matter which influences the direction and rate of neutrino distribution. Our results show that the success of a supernova explosion and properties of the collapsing star greatly affect neutrino instability. Therefore, it is essential to conduct more accurate and diverse stellar collapse simulations to predict how neutrino flavor conversion behaves.

ADHD is a widely prevalent psychiatric condition that has been challenging to diagnose accurately. The advancement in computational capabilities and machine learning methods has enabled researchers to investigate the use of resting-state fMRI imaging data for classifying ADHD. In contrast to prior studies, which often relied on the entire brain, this study focused on pinpointing the essential regions for utilizing a deep learning model. By using rsfMRI data from the ADHD 200 global competition, the researchers employed leave-one-site-out cross-validation to derive an integrated outcome. Notably, the study found that using merely 15 crucial regions of interest for training yielded a 70.6% accuracy rate, surpassing the existing benchmark of 68.6% achieved with all regions. Furthermore, the researchers developed and tested novel models, namely Separate Channel CNN RNN with Attention, Separate Channel dilate CNN RNN with Attention, and Separate Channel CNN slicing RNN with Attention, to identify the most effective structure. The ASSRNN model emerged as the top performer, attaining a 70.46% accuracy rate with only 13 essential regions. The study's findings demonstrate that concentrating on the critical brain regions for ADHD diagnosis via deep learning can yield superior outcomes compared to using the entire brain.

In a discrete-time epidemic SISI model where population growth is constant and balanced, the per capita mortality and fertility rates are equivalent, and the model's evolution operator is a nonlinear function of seven parameters. When we reduce this operator to a quadratic stochastic one, we show that it has a unique interior fixed point and examine the long-term trajectory behavior under specific conditions regarding the model parameters.

Acronyms and abbreviations serve as shorter versions of lengthy phrases, commonly found across diverse writing mediums. While they are instrumental in saving space and time in written communication, they also introduce comprehension hurdles if not clearly defined, particularly if the acronym's origin is unclear in lengthy texts. To address this, concerted efforts from both researchers and software developers are directed at creating systems capable of automatically processing and interpreting acronyms. Unfortunately, existing solutions have limited scope, targeting either acronym definition extraction or translation, but not the broader challenge. To overcome this, a unified approach is proposed, incorporating a proprietary acronym database to facilitate a comprehensive system. The database-enhanced system is capable of identifying undefined acronyms in context, extracting and defining new acronyms, and translating established ones. The proposed solution is exemplified through two case studies, one focusing on academic writing and the other on technical translation.

Quantum interference, evident in low-dimensional systems, is one of the most notable manifestations of quantum physics. Historically, quantum interference has been observed in charge transport; however, recent findings indicate that it also significantly affects thermal properties. This insight enables the precise manipulation of heat within microscopic devices through phase-coherence. This study showcases how exploiting phase-coherent edge states in quantum Hall systems allows for the realization of exceptional thermoelectric properties and efficient heat rectification. A multi-quantum point contact tunneling experiment was conducted to examine these effects. Our investigation examined tunneling conductance and thermoelectric properties as complete phase coherence was established. We observed heat rectification in which the same contact could either transfer heat or insulate against it, depending on the relative alignment of the contacts' phases. We further demonstrated that by adjusting this phase, the heat rectification could be fine-tuned to optimize heat or charge conductivity. These findings open doors for the utilization of quantum Hall systems in advanced heat management technologies.

Our proposed DNA-storage system presents a new, flexible structure that establishes a hierarchical relationship among data objects identified by the same primer pair and facilitates efficient data revisions. Unlike existing approaches, in this architecture a pair of twenty base PCR primers no longer defines a singular object, but rather a distinct, independently managed storage segment with its own index. We've discovered that, although there are limited discrete addresses in the PCR primers space, it's feasible to create massive, uniquely indexed datasets from it by utilizing hybridization-induced cascades of locus expansion. Furthermore, we've developed an algorithm allowing segment index creation and found that focusing on data redundancy and error correction requirements enables significant reduction in required base pairs per segment. We've implemented this new structure in two existing DNA-storage systems and conducted tests, which demonstrated an approximate hundredfold increase in address space, along with improved data organization and update capabilities.

Topological insulators represent a significant phenomenon in modern physics, characterized by exceptional properties of exotic states that facilitate unidirectional and unobstructed electron flow and protect the system from external influences by enabling a full spectral spin-Hall plateau. Current research has revealed that incorporating magnetism into these systems can greatly augment their properties. Although the introduction of magnetism is beneficial, controlling and directing the topological insulator's electronic properties remains challenging due to their inherently disordered nature. To overcome this limitation, we have successfully demonstrated the precise control of the electrical flow and the detection of hidden electronic properties within a device comprised of a topological insulator and magnetism, utilizing an ultra-thin film made from the magnet BixSe2xTe1-x. Our research has achieved the integration of controlled external stimuli and the manipulation of magnetic orientation to exploit the full potential of topological insulators, opening up new avenues for practical applications in quantum technology.

In oscillatory media, regions that oscillate faster than their surroundings can give rise to outgoing waves, which are crucial for synchronization across entire systems. We examine this phenomenon in a specific type of oscillatory medium, focusing on the effects of oscillatory shocks and pacemaker-generated waves within turbulent systems. Our research, conducted using the reduced view of the Klausmeier-Schwab model, reveals how pacemakers, situated at the system's boundary, induce synchronized oscillations throughout the system. The resulting oscillations often take the form of uniform oscillations or alternating phases between oscillating and non-oscillating states. The former can give rise to outgoing waves, whereas the latter may give rise to the disappearance of pacemakers or the formation of oscillating patterns, determined by the system's distance from the pacemaker and the pacemaker's size and oscillation frequency.

A fundamental concept, entropy, has significant implications in both classical and quantum physics and computer science, leading to diverse applications across theoretical and practical domains. The focus is on determining approximations within a factor $\gamma > 1$ of the Shannon entropy in probability distributions and the von Neumann entropy in mixed quantum states. The key contributions are two algorithms: a quantum one for approximating Shannon entropy that requires $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^{\frac{1+\eta}{2\gamma^2}})$ queries, and another for approximating von Neumann entropy that necessitates $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^{\frac{1+\eta}{2\gamma^2}+s}$ queries, with $s \leq \min\{\log N, \frac{1}{\gamma^2} \}$, thereby establishing the first quantum algorithm for solving this problem. The results are further bolstered by lower bounds, demonstrating that these algorithms are nearly optimal, with marginal sub-optimality due to the implementation of quantum approximation algorithms. The introduced techniques are anticipated to yield further significant outcomes in the quantum computing domain.

Implementing and deploying effective artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, necessitates substantial datasets for training, testing, and validation processes. Establishing comprehensive data collections, annotated in accordance with standardized protocols, necessitates the setup of imaging biobanks to ensure organized access. Achieving this, however, involves intricate design, careful compliance with current regulatory frameworks and technical standards. Simply collecting and storing imaging data does not suffice; high computational requirements necessitate an intelligent synergy between on-premise infrastructure and cloud computing to deploy AI pipelines. This chapter serves as a resource, providing technical context and insights into essential concepts and implementations regarding data storage, cloud integration, and AI pipeline orchestration to inform readers about pivotal technical decisions.

Physicians' written assessments and interviews with patients, stored as unstructured clinical text notes (CTNs), have been analyzed by recent studies using machine learning techniques to forecast diagnoses based on CTNs, a task known as International Classification of Diseases (ICD) coding. Researchers have addressed ICD coding as a separate task or combined it with diagnosis prediction, utilizing deep learning models and datasets originating from natural language processing (NLP) competitions. To address these limitations, we redrafted the coding task to fit medical professionals' standard diagnostic procedures and developed a new data set, DDI_NHS, reflecting real-world clinicians' practices. Our study compares the performance of the deep learning models and the newly created data set with the conventional benchmarks, concluding with recommendations for future research.

Let $R$ be a polynomial ring in $n$ variables over a field $k$. A monomial ideal $I$ within this ring is considered. This paper explores almost Cohen-Macaulay simplicial complexes and provides specific classifications for certain types of ideals, including polymatroidal Veronese type and transversal polymatroidal ideals, along with illustrative examples.

Due to the diverse applications of machine learning, its ability to identify patterns in datasets is well-established, albeit limited by the rapid growth of computation time with dataset size. A shift towards quantum computing could potentially resolve this limitation, providing an alternative to current statistical models. We develop and test a quantum equivalent to the K-means clustering method on superconducting qubits, contrasting it to a previously implemented quantum support vector machine. Results indicate that our algorithm matches classical K-means performance in both clustering and classification tasks, achieving an impressive speedup due to a lower asymptotic complexity of $O(N^{3/2}K^{1/2})$ with $N$ and $K$ representing the number of data points and clusters, respectively.

Our analysis encompasses all prime-field microlensing planets from the 2018 dataset provided by the KMTNet AnomalyFinder, revealing 24 total discoveries or recoveries - ten previously unpublished planets with definitive or probable planetary nature: KMT-2018-BLG-2004, OGLE-2018-BLG-1126, and seven other identified planets; combined with four AnomalyFinder-confirmed new planets from published data, and twelve discovered by visual examination. Together, a study detailing sub-prime planet findings is set to complement our findings. Using the method outlined by Hwang et al. (2022), a modification is introduced to their formalism to remove close/wide and inner/outer degeneracies discrepancies.

Differentiable rendering has gained significant attention in image-based inverse problems due to its potential to enhance traditional optimization-based methods and offer self-supervision for learning-based approaches, particularly those lacking ground truth-annotated training data. However, existing differentiable renderers are either limited by their failure to account for light sources or only work on specific object categories. To address these issues, we introduce an advanced differentiable renderer that incorporates the Blinn-Phong lighting model and a general layout that can represent various objects, such as car parts, traffic scenes, and human faces with accessories. By employing this new renderer, we accelerate two inverse problems: 3D pose estimation and facial animation. Our results demonstrate superior performance compared to the current best techniques. Furthermore, this research serves as a platform for the development of new learning algorithms informed by optical flow, novel view synthesis, and image translation.

Recent research on transportation networks has highlighted the need to account for uncertainty and reliability by modeling the probability of origin-destination demand and network flow. Building on the work of Kaushal and Jammalamadaka, we continue this research by examining how sampling variances relate to chosen measurement locations within a network. The study measures this relationship through two traffic counts, where the variance of estimated traffic flow includes the effects of non-stationary traffic and the probability of misclassifying traffic volumes. The results show that sampling variances are highest at nodes with the highest traffic volumes and the widest range of travel times.

In an array of nonlinear oscillators with random frequencies and purely conserved interactions, global phase coherence is demonstrated to occur within finite networks and further examined as it collapses through the generation of localized periodic and chaotic waves following a parameter adjustment. For weak nonlinearity in the system, these global phases exhibit a temporary state of stability, akin to that observed in nearly conservative systems. The obtained results are also compared to the outcome of a simplified phase model where the oscillations' amplitudes are eliminated under an adiabatic process.

The well-documented Aldous-Broder and Wilson algorithms create random spanning trees through random walks, and this research examines their synergy with the aim of reducing tree construction time. Demonstrating statistical equivalence on particular stopping points by analyzing 'branches' produced by these algorithms shows that an earlier method can be utilized to generate uniform spanning trees at a faster rate. This new method leverages the outcomes of the existing algorithms to expedite the generation of additional tree components. Consequently, a linear-time uniform spanning tree generation method is developed, and this study further explores spanning forest generation via a similar approach.

This work presents a comprehensive music dataset named MusicTM-Dataset that enhances cross-modal retrieval capabilities by offering a diverse collection of multimedia data. Currently, large music datasets featuring three modalities are scarce, limiting the ability to learn effective representations for cross-modal applications. To bridge this gap, our research expands on existing musical notation, combining it with audio synthesis and generated sheet-music images to create a dataset with precise alignments among audio, visual, and text-based components. This aligned MusicTM-Dataset allows for the development of unified representations across multimodal data points. Comprising sheet-music images, lyrical text, and synthesized audio, the dataset is constructed from various sources, offering a broad spectrum of musical styles spanning from classical to pop. This work presents our method for generating musical notation from text, our experience in training an automatic singing voice synthesizer, and our approach to image generation using text, all of which contribute to a comprehensive music dataset. To facilitate reproducibility, our research includes a detailed description of our dataset creation process, as well as publicly accessible code and data downloads, specifically through the Reproducible Finance Initiative's GitHub repository under the open-source OSQM project. This work does not receive any financial benefit.

One major obstacle when utilizing Linked Data lies in developing intuitive and user-friendly interfaces accessible to individuals who aren't technologically inclined. To address this, Ontodia enables diagrammatic data visualization, illustrated in this study with the Wikidata dataset. We've introduced enhancements to a natural language interface that facilitates the exploration and querying of Linked Data entities. By utilizing distributional semantic models to identify and rank entity properties associated with user input in Ontodia, the method demonstrates improved results in enhancing user experience during visual data exploration.

We've discovered that in the nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation with variable refractive index and a defocusing cubic nonlinearity, dark solitons display the same characteristics as in the pure cubic defocusing model. However, adding variable refractive index significantly changes how we assess stability in the dark solitons. Notably, only isolated imaginary axis eigenvalues are found, and energy-based stability is applicable. Moreover, both short- and long-range bound states, known as ring solitons, are stable when the system has a defocusing nonlinearity. The research also shows that in a certain range of variable refractive index, solitons with features similar to "black" solitons can be stable.

This collaborative approach in visual analytics focuses on guiding human analysts with actionable suggestions, tailored to their expertise and current work.  To facilitate seamless interaction, we introduce the concept of relative guidance - the ability to provide suggestions relative to the analyst's previous actions, as recorded by the system.  This relative guidance approach is implemented as a general framework comprising three core components: analyzing the analyst's behavior, identifying significant trends, and formulating actionable suggestions.  We illustrate the effectiveness of this method in two distinct scenarios: browsing through thousands of images and exploring vast literary databases.

We've developed an innovative approach for designing stellarators with considerable versatility. Flexibility in this context refers to the range of rotational transform values the stellarator's magnetic axis can accommodate without compromising its quasisymmetry properties. Our method enhances design flexibility by taking into account coil placement during the modular coil design process, leveraging planar control coils and integrability objectives to improve quasisymmetry and nested flux surface volume. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by optimizing a coil set inspired by NCSX design, which not only achieves a range of rotational transform values but also surpasses the NCSX design in nested flux surface volume.

Achieving uniform temperature distribution within catalytic fixed bed reactors is critical for both optimal production yield and operational stability.  However, obtaining precise temperature readings simultaneously with good spatial and temporal resolution in these systems remains difficult. Our research utilizes the capabilities of real-time MRI imaging in conjunction with the temperature-dependent shift in water's proton resonance frequency to obtain in situ temperature measurements in a cylindrical fixed bed reactor. The temperature distribution was monitored as the reactor was heated from room temperature to 60°C using hot air, with three-dimensional temperature maps produced every two seconds. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of this non-invasive thermometry technique for understanding mass and heat transfer in fixed bed systems.

Within a cellular environment, proteins and nucleic acids autonomously separate, resulting in the spontaneous formation of membraneless droplets. This process underlies the development of numerous sub-cellular compartments. In a model system designed to understand condensate self-assembly, interactions between a large number of different molecular species were studied and programmed to test for variability and rules. The number of different droplets formed from mixtures increased significantly as the number of different molecular species in the mixtures increased. The maximum number of different droplets in a mixture could be accurately predicted even without full knowledge of all interactions. The models' simulations confirmed these expectations and suggested the underlying rules for spatial organization through droplets could be widely applied across cellular molecular mixtures.

Using the Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager on the Solar Dynamics Observatory, we studied how a major leading sunspot rotated in NOAA AR 11429 during two powerful solar flares. A notable sunspot rotated in an unconventional direction, influenced significantly by the solar eruptions. Moving disturbances within other sunspots, caused by the solar flares, traveled rapidly and altered the magnetic properties associated with the sunspots in question, providing valuable insights into the dynamic process governing the sunspots' development.

This note presents a new category of map functions known as oriented colored broken submersions, which forms the most basic type of map functions that adhere to the b-principle, and is nearly equivalent to the set of oriented submersions in 2 dimensions. It demonstrates that the Madsen-Weiss theorem, which can be viewed as a variation of the standard Mumford Conjecture, is derivable from a specific application of the b-principle to oriented colored broken submersions, combined with the findings from Harer's stability theorem and Miller and Morita's work.

This research involves comparing the efficiency of Balancing Domain Decomposition by Constraints (BDDC) and Algebraic Multigrid (AMG) methods for solving complex cardiac mechanics problems on various types of finite element grids. By modeling the mechanical properties of heart muscle tissue using three-dimensional finite elasticity equations, researchers have transformed the problem into a nonlinear algebraic system. A combination of Newton-Krylov and BDDC/AMG solvers is employed to solve this large system. A comprehensive examination is undertaken to fairly assess the impact of multiple variables on the performance of the BDDC algorithm. Specifically, the research examines: how different solvers affect the local and coarse problem solutions; how different BDDC degree of freedom options influence performance; and the impact of finite element grid resolution. Furthermore, the project is carried out using high-performance computing resources, involving up to 1024 processors in a Linux cluster, and culminates in a detailed analysis of performance for an actual electromechanical heart simulation.

The ever-growing influence of user-generated content is significantly altering the digital landscape, driven in part by the proliferation of systems supporting content creation, sharing, and management. Among these systems are tag-based platforms that enable users to collaborate in annotating shared items such as images and URLs, leading to user-generated metadata pools and collaborative behavior. To unlock this potential, a comprehensive understanding of current systems is required, which involves characterizing these systems based on usage patterns, the evolution of user-generated content over time, and the underlying social dynamics.

Recently, proposed bianisotropic acoustic metagratings offer promising possibilities for passive acoustic devices that could increase the availability and quality of ultrasound imaging by focusing unfocused beams and enhancing resolution. Unlike conventional isotropic devices, bianisotropic metagratings can manipulate polarization, thus allowing various unit cells with built-in rotation angles to create designed acoustic waves. Nevertheless, the proposed acoustic metagratings face a significant challenge of achieving reliable numerical modeling due to their complex structure. This study presents a novel numerical modeling approach for a specific type of bianisotropic metagrating and demonstrates its effectiveness through comparison with experimental and numerical issues in the literature. The proposed method shows significant potential to expand the scope of acoustic metagratings and advance their application in fields like ultrasound imaging and medical imaging.

This paper primarily focuses on the long-term behavior of strong solutions to the two-dimensional compressible FENE dumbbell model. Utilizing the Fourier splitting technique, we demonstrate that the $L^2$ decay rate is given by $\ln^{-l}(e+t)$, with any positive integer $l$. Through the application of the time-weighted energy method, we manage to enhance this rate to $(1+t)^{-\frac{1}{4}}$. Under the condition that the frequencies are sufficiently low, by incorporating the principles of the Littlewood-Paley theory, we find that the solutions have properties belonging to certain Besov spaces of negative order and establish the most favorable $L^2$ decay rate.

Implementing integrated access and backhaul (IAB) through wireless connections offers a promising way to develop flexible and high-density networks. Mobile IAB, which facilitates the connection of UEs in motion, holds potential as a suitable solution. This work takes a different approach from existing literature by providing a comprehensive overview of deploying mobile IAB by covering: the IAB standardization in 5G New Radio (NR); a classification framework for both fixed and mobile IAB; an extensive analysis of mobile IAB performance through simulations; and the open challenges and potential prospects of this technology. The proposed taxonomy organizes existing IAB research by categorizing different perspectives, while categorizing mobile IAB by the type of mobility involved. In terms of performance assessment, the authors analyzed mobile IAB deployments in urban environments, specifically buses to enhance passenger connectivity, which resulted in significantly improved throughput and latency in both downlink and uplink compared to other network configurations.

In this study, we conduct an extensive examination of five leading global optimization algorithms as a hyperparameter configuration problem to understand the overall impact of their settings on performance. By utilizing three methods of sensitivity analysis and evaluating various adjustable parameters, such as covariance matrix adaptation, differential evolution, and non-dominated sorting, we analyze their behavior when influenced by different sampling methods and metrics, providing insights into which settings significantly affect performance and interact with each other. The ranking of influential parameters suggests an optimal order of tuning, and our results also shed light on the overall stability of the algorithms.

The paper addresses misconceptions surrounding Jefimenko's equations, which are derived from Maxwell's equations, for a specific charge and current configuration obeying the continuity equation. It subsequently derives a non-radiative condition across inertial frames, consistent with the stability requirements of an atom, and then establishes a fundamental relationship between the Lorentz force and the product of charge, velocity, and acceleration. Finally, the paper demonstrates that these relationships lead to the classical Thomas precession formula and explains the apparent discrepancies in relation to the classical radius of the proton.

Despite notable breakthroughs in reinforcement learning, numerous significant hurdles remain when applying it to dynamic and ever-changing problems common in critical domains, including robotics and complex gameplay. Reinforcement learning models often struggle to generalize effectively when confronted with new tasks beyond their training data. In response to this challenge, the field is seeing an increased focus on continual learning methods, and to support this research, new tools are being developed, including carefully crafted evaluation frameworks and benchmark environments. To address this need, we present Lifelong Learning Explorer (L2Explorer), a cutting-edge Unity-based environment that allows for continuous, flexible experimentation in a 3D, immersive exploration setting. L2Explorer is distinct from procedurally generated worlds, which often incorporate randomized components. Instead, we've developed a structured and systematic approach to creating learning curricula in response to controlled changes, along with complementary metrics to assess transfer, performance, and search efficiency. The comprehensive framework and methodology we've established with L2Explorer provide a crucial platform for advancing future evaluation methods and rigorous assessment of lifelong learning strategies.

Liger, a next-generation infrared device at the W. M. Keck Observatory, will be paired with the Keck All-sky Precision Adaptive-optics system to optimize performance. By covering the wavelength range from 0.81 micrometers to 2.45 micrometers, Liger combines multiple observing modes, offering various spatial scales and fields of view. However, Liger's data complexity necessitates a customized data processing system to refine its output in real-time, making it compatible with science-oriented data presentation tools. This processing system, called the Data Reduction System, will be responsible for delivering refined data to astronomers and uploading it to the Keck Observatory Archive. We are currently developing the Data Reduction System, which will utilize Python-based tools and follow established protocols to minimize implementation challenges.

This study uncovers a broad class of non-trivial and smooth travelling waves that arise in the vicinity of the Couette flow in 2D Euler equation, at low regularity in vorticity $H^s$ for $s<3$. The velocity of these waves is directly proportional to their distance from the Couette flow. This finding significantly deviates from scenarios involving Gevrey spaces, where the radius of analysis limits the size of the perturbation. This research implies a drastic change in behaviour as the regularity threshold in vorticity increases.

We experimentally control the linear polarization of exciton-polariton condensates using optical traps with elliptical geometries that favor specific polarization modes. Due to anisotropic splitting in the cavity, ground state degeneracy is lifted, yielding fine structure modes along the trap's axis and orthogonal to it. These modes are selectively occupied by the condensate. Our results reveal a method for polarization control with potential applications in spin-based photonics and research on complex optical systems with adjustable coupling properties.

This study's primary objective is to provide evidence and disproofs for the deterministic Kardar-Parisi-Zhang type equations including non-local gradient elements. The specific focus lies within a particular class of nonlocal problems formulated within a given domain in higher dimensions. The formulation is based on an equation where the fractional Laplacian of a variable $u$ is equal to the sum of a nonlinear term that involves the norm of the variable's gradient and an additional parameter with an applied force function. The conditions of existence and non-existence are explored with varying coefficients in a specific mathematical framework and solutions to related problems from earlier works are provided.

The  COVID-19 pandemic, triggered by SARS-CoV-2 in 2020, was officially classified as a global health crisis by the WHO. As a result, the world is relying heavily on public health precautions such as social distancing measures to curb the virus spread and maintain the healthcare system functionality. With the isolation of communities, access to reliable information has become restricted. Consequently, the health minister in South Africa updates the public every day on COVID-19 infections, including affected individuals' demographic and travel details. Meanwhile, the National Institute for Communicable Diseases provides daily updates on testing numbers, case counts, and fatality rates via infographics but often fails to release patients' ages or other critical transmission details. Recognizing the need to effectively share this information, the University of Pretoria's Data Science for Social Impact research team developed an open-access data platform to centralize and streamline COVID-19 data reporting. This initiative leverages data science capabilities to process, integrate, and display data from multiple sources, featuring user-friendly data visualizations tailored to mobile devices. This endeavour aims to aid the South African government in maintaining data transparency by consistently updating the public with reliable, visual information. Furthermore, the platform may serve as a valuable resource for researchers pursuing vaccine efficacy, infectiousness, and other critical aspects of COVID-19.

Freiman's 3k-4 theorem generally posits that if subsets A and B, of size k and comprised of integers, share a sumset with a size near 2k, then A and B exhibit considerable similarity to arithmetic progressions. In this paper, we aim to enhance this by limiting the number of possible summands available from subset B. It's shown that if subsets A and B, of size k, meet the criterion that for every four-element subset of B, the sumset A plus that subset doesn't exceed 2k, it follows that A and B exhibit considerable similarity to arithmetic progressions.

In medical contexts, diverse information often arises from various sources, which when combined enables healthcare professionals to form more precise opinions. For retinal analysis in particular, recent advancements have led to increased use of multiple imaging methods: standard two-dimensional fundus photographs and more detailed three-dimensional imaging techniques such as optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography. Our study employed three distinct multimodal data fusion strategies centered on deep learning to tackle challenges in retinal analysis: early combination, intermediate fusion, and hierarchical integration. Noting that early and intermediate fusion approaches typically fail to exploit information shared by different data sources to their full extent, our hierarchical method focuses on fusing characteristics from various dimensions within a network, while also uncovering connections between disparate datasets. We implemented these strategies on classification tasks involving glaucoma and diabetic retinopathy using a range of standard datasets and proprietary OCT data, which demonstrated the superior performance of our hierarchical method.

X-ray images contain subtle characteristics with predictive information about patients who are likely to experience severe COVID-19 symptoms.  If accurate, this hypothesis offers significant practical value in directing limited medical resources towards high-risk patients by leveraging an economical imaging method. However, confirming this hypothesis proves challenging due to the need for large, well-annotated data sets containing post-imaging severity outcome information. To address this issue, a novel approach is proposed for extracting crucial features from datasets with only death outcomes by utilizing lung area segmentation to eliminate background noise during image characterization. Furthermore, this study explores the effectiveness of using multiple neural network architectures to detect these features and compares the performance of training models using lung area segmentation images with that of training models using unsegmented X-ray images. The results show that the proposed method outperforms standard training approaches, and when applied to 119 separate hospital datasets, model versions trained on X-ray images with automated lung area segmentation achieve a 74% accuracy rate in predicting severe COVID-19 cases.

We analyze the transmission eigenvalue problem involving $u$ and $v$ in the Sobolev space $H^1(\Omega)$ associated with $(\Omega, \sigma, \mathbf{n}^2)$. Considering the case where $\Omega$ is a 2 or 3-dimensional ball, and the functions $\sigma$ and $\mathbf{n}$ only depend on the radial distance $r$, we find a sequence of transmission eigenfunctions that tend to concentrate their energies around the boundary of $\Omega$ as the associated wavenumbers $k$ increase without bound. If $\sigma$ and $\mathbf{n}$ are constant, we prove the existence of transmission eigenfunctions that become localized around the boundary of $\Omega$. Our results generalize the recent studies in the mentioned literature and also illustrate the influence of medium parameters $\sigma$ and $\mathbf{n}$ on the geometric patterns of transmission eigenfunctions via numerical experiments.

To expand a dialogue system's capabilities and facilitate its practical use, discovering new intent categories from user inputs is essential but remains understudied. Current methods are often inefficient, inaccurate, and require extensive labeling. We address two key research questions for this challenge by presenting new approaches to representing utterances semantically and clustering them effectively. Firstly, we develop a pre-trained encoder tailored to aggregate multiple token features across various datasets. Secondly, we introduce a group-wise, self-supervised pre-training strategy to prepare representations for task-specific fine-tuning. Experiments on two benchmark datasets demonstrate the superiority of our method over existing approaches in both new intent discovery and traditional classification tasks.

The classical universal bundle functor W maps from the category of simplicial groups in C to the category of simplicial sets in C, and it can be generalized to map from the category of simplicial algebras in C to the category of simplicial sets in C. Given a commutative ring R, the Lie algebras over R can be represented as subalgebras of the free Lie algebra on a set M in C, and this scenario extends the universal bundle functor W to map from the category of Lie algebras in C to the category of simplicial sets in C. Additionally, for a commutative ring R, the Lie algebras in C can be described as Lie algebras on R-bounded simplicial sets, and this description allows for the representation of a universal cofibration sequence in the category of Lie algebras in C. Similarly, for a commutative ring R, the Lie algebras in C can be described as Lie algebras on R-bounded simplicial sets, and this description allows for the derivation of a universal fibration sequence in the category of Lie algebras in C. Also, the general form of the universal fibration sequence in the category of Lie algebras in C can be expressed as a specific algebraic equation involving the universal bundle functor W, and this equation may be of use in modeling algebraic structures as subalgebras of Lie algebras
In our analysis, we demonstrate that a finite group of order $r$ possesses no more than $$7.3722\cdot r^{\frac{\log_2r}{4}+1.5315}$$ subgroups.

This study re-examines the Adler-Bobenko-Suris H2 equation. The equation has a direct linear relationship with the Cauchy matrix scheme variables defined by S. Shabat and Y. Stsepanou, and these variables can be described using 3D consistency conditions. A lattice Yang-Baxter equation is formulated based on these variables, and a specific inverse scattering transform is proposed. The inverse scattering method is linked to a Whitham-type nonlinear Shrodinger equation. Additionally, the paper mentions connections to quantum inverse scattering and conformal field theory.

This paper delves into the source of high false positive rates in Visual Relationship Detection (VRD). During training, we discovered that the relationship proposal distribution is skewed, with the majority of incorrect relationships being easily identified due to poor object detection. As a result, low-frequency difficult proposals struggle to contribute effectively. Our proposed framework, Spatially-Aware Balanced Negative Proposal Sampling (SABRA), mitigates the impact of false positives in VRD tasks. To counter the imbalance, SABRA incorporates Balanced Negative Proposal Sampling (BNPS), which divides proposals into distinct sub-classes based on difficulty and samples a balanced distribution accordingly. By employing this strategy, BNPS yields an optimized model performance and a notable decrease in false positives. To further address the challenging low-frequency proposals, we introduce Spatially-Aware BNPS (SABNPS), which segments the image into non-overlapping regions and applies BNPS within each space, selectively suppressing false proposals in each region. Our method demonstrates superior performance compared to the current state-of-the-art approaches on three VRD benchmarks, achieving significant improvements of 3.3%, 5.3%, and 2.6% in relation proposal accuracy, with notable gains in object and relationship detection accuracy as well.

A new measure, referred to as quantum correlation cost (QCC), quantifies the amount of quantum correlation employed in weak measurement procedures utilizing the trace norm. It's demonstrated that the QCC is directly linked to the trace-norm-based quantum discord (TQD) by a factor dependent on weak measurement strength. However, this measure only captures a portion of a quantum system's quantum nature in comparison to the TQD. Furthermore, research finds that remaining quantum features can be extracted not only via further von Neumann measurements but also through a series of infinitesimally weak measurements. This outcome is validated through both theoretical analysis and a quantum simulation.

Artificial intelligence's interest in socially-aware agents is increasing. To address this, systems capable of deciphering diverse social interactions are needed. Understanding social relationships in a visual setting requires not only object recognition but also an in-depth comprehension of socially-connected objects and actions. An explicit knowledge graph can be employed to model social connections and facilitate scene analysis. In this research paper, we introduce Social Relationship Graph, an explicit graph model, to represent socially-connected objects and actions. We also introduce Social Relationship Graph PreTrained, a novel pre-training framework that pretrains node and edge embeddings through contrastive learning. This enables existing models that utilize graph models to enhance their performance by simply replacing their current graph representations with the Social Relationship Graph PreTrained. Experimental results demonstrate Social Relationship Graph PreTrained significantly boosts performance on existing social datasets, yielding near state-of-the-art performance on DSD80 and Kinetics-SRN and set a new benchmark on Social Genome Action Recognition and Social Genome Action Recognition with partial annotations.

Capturing long-range relationships in scene understanding tasks is a crucial goal in computer vision. While CNNs excel in many vision tasks, they have limitations in modelling global, structured representations due to their localized nature. Self-attention methods, introduced in NLP, can easily fall victim to attention 'blight' at scale. Graph neural networks have shown promise in modelling global structures but often rely on manually assembled graphs, which can be impractical in many computer vision tasks. Our work introduces the dynamic graph message passing network, enabling automatic creation and refinement of scene graphs from image features alone. This is achieved through a novel graph construction method, using a directed graph, where nodes represent image regions and edges represent perceived relationships. Edge weights are calculated by a binary classifier, predicting presence or absence of an edge, and a sub-graph refinement process enhances the representation of detected relationships. The DGMPN is training-free after the initial stage and requires no manual assembly of the graph. Our experiments show the DGMPN leads to significant improvements in model size and processing speed while achieving state-of-the-art performance in predicting image relationships and object categorisation, and notably outperforms other methods in predicting graph node properties, particularly for smaller objects.

Optimized hardware is often required in embedded systems, leading to a common operation called Multiple Constant Multiplication (MCM) over integers. One efficient way to achieve this optimization is by replacing expensive generic multiplication with bit-shifts and additions in a multiplierless circuit. Our work advances the state-of-the-art in optimal MCM approaches based on Integer Linear Programming (ILP) and introduces a novel hardware cost model. This model counts one-bit adders, demonstrating a strong correlation with the number of LUTs required. Our enhanced model accommodates intermediate precision truncations, enabling significant resource savings when full precision is not essential. Additionally, we incorporate error propagation rules to ensure a specified error margin for MCM results. Our proposed ILP models for various MCM configurations are available in an open-source tool, integrated with the FloPoCo VHDL code generator, providing a complete flow from coefficients to hardware design. Thorough experiments were conducted to assess the models, followed by a detailed analysis of how design metrics impact actual hardware implementation.

The intersection of quantum computing and deep neural networks has recently given rise to a growing research field, known as quantum deep learning. Despite previously being separate entities, advancements have revealed that quantum circuits share parallels with artificial neural networks, paving the way for widespread adoption. This paper delves into the foundational aspects and core principles of quantum deep learning, highlighting key breakthroughs along the way. It also explores the challenges inherent in quantum deep learning research from multiple viewpoints, followed by a discussion of prospective future directions and practical applications.

The radio frequency (RF) accelerator technology continues to be fundamental in 
high-energy physics (HEP) experiments, where significant progress has been 
made over the past decade in advancing the field. This progress could soon lead 
to upgraded existing facilities, enhancements to facilities still under 
construction (such as PIP-II), well-established proposals, or newly emerging 
ideas like the FCC-ee and future proton intensity upgrade at Fermilab, among 
others. Innovations in RF technology not only contribute to HEP but also extend 
beyond to fields such as nuclear physics, basic energy sciences, and other areas, 
as evidenced by European XFEL, LCLS-II and related facilities, or SHINE, 
EIC, and FRIB. Therefore, an extensive R&D program focusing on RF technology 
is needed to tackle challenges in accelerator-based applications and introduce 
new, promising technologies.

In the near future, physicists anticipate that the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) will discover new physics. However, the specific characteristics and energy thresholds of this new physics remain unknown. It's probable that insights gleaned from LHC data will require supplementary information obtained from a lepton collider to conduct a thorough investigation. This text discusses the underlying principles, accelerator layout, and detector development for a high-energy Muon Collider as well as the difficulties inherent in the new physics investigation at energies approaching 3 TeV.

We have determined the dispersion relations for relativistic fluid modes in various configurations - scalar, vector, and tensor - and found that their behavior differs significantly in extreme situations. In extreme conditions, these modes diverge, with both hydrodynamic and non-hydrodynamic modes exhibiting unusual, highly dispersive characteristics. These findings suggest that relativistic fluid modes may serve as effective probes for extreme environment research.

Our research assesses whether the cosmic background of Hawking radiation from primordial black holes could be the source behind the observed excess radiowave signals. By assuming that dark matter exists entirely as these black holes, we calculated that the temperature resulting from Hawking radiation is insufficient to produce the observed excess signals, an insight supported by simple mathematical arguments. This deficiency is due to the constraints imposed by cosmic microwave background measurements. Although black holes are vastly more numerous than stars, a significant portion of their energy is lost due to curvature radiation, a process that hinders the amplitude of Hawking radiation. Nevertheless, future radio telescopes with significantly enhanced sensitivity may be able to verify whether the cosmic background of Hawking radiation equals the thermal noise generated by the cosmic microwave background.

Introducing the Virtual Secure Platform (VSP), a pioneering solution that brings together multi-opcode general-purpose sequential processing with Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) to enable Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC) at a secure computing offloading level, such as cloud computing. The VSP safeguardingly shields both input data and function evaluations against adversaries in a secure computing offloading scenario like cloud computing. To enhance performance, our innovative VSP architecture features a five-stage pipeline design that increases circuit evaluation parallelism. Moreover, a custom-designed Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) was created to decrease processor gate count, accompanied by comprehensive toolchains for ISA testing and development. To further boost performance, CMU CMP-8 type processor cores were integrated to achieve full pipeline circuit evaluation through multi-core parallel processing. To evaluate the VSP's performance, a 128-bit instruction ISA was implemented, alongside common mathematical opcode function evaluations, to compare its efficiency with existing similar processors. Finally, a Secure Circuit Construction (SCC) method was used to construct secure circuits that reflect actual SMPC computations to verify the VSP's throughput and power consumption. Consequently, the results showed that the VSP achieved superior performance compared to current processors in both security mode and non-security mode scenarios.

Researchers investigate polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTAS) for solving specific constraint satisfaction problems, such as Maximum Independent Set or Minimum Vertex Cover on graph classes that have limited connectivity.

A previously developed approach by Baker achieved PTAS on various graph classes including planar graphs. Further, Romero, Wrochna, and Zivny developed a simpler PTAS for certain graph classes using the Sherali-Adams LP relaxation for maximum CSPs with constraints defined by arbitrary non-negative functions.

This research is extended to CSPs with constraints that have multiple possible values. The only restriction for such constraints is that they contain an element that is at least as acceptable as all other elements.

A new PTAS is presented for general-valued CSPs with constraints that have distinct values, such as 0 and 1, but with specific limitations. The technique was previously applicable to classes where Baker's approach worked, but now also allows for more flexible general-valued CSPs on certain graph classes.

Pre-trained language models possess the ability to capture syntactic information, as seen in the performance achieved by simply fine-tuning them for parsing tasks. However, the underlying syntactic features in these models are obscure, making it challenging to modify them. To unveil the syntactic capabilities of these models, we employ linear projections to transform query and key vectors in the self-attention mechanism, allowing us to extract dimension-specific syntactic patterns. Notably, the resulting projections surpass the performance of unsupervised syntactic representations extracted from pre-trained models through autoencoder-based methods. Additionally, we discover that combining our method with the established BERT-dependent unsupervised parsing techniques yields significant gains, ultimately attaining performance comparable to supervised methods on various parsing tasks.

High-definition hyperspectral images possess the unique capability to distinguish between diverse objects within intricate environments by analyzing each pixel across various frequency ranges. Although HSI cameras are becoming increasingly accessible, associated algorithms have not been extensively utilized. This research delves into a novel application, employing hyperspectral images for cityscape object segmentation using an unsupervised learning approach that circumvents the need for manual object classification. This method capitalizes on the rich spectral data inherent in HSI images, which facilitates efficient object segmentation within complex urban environments. By analyzing the inherent properties of HSI images and developing corresponding processing techniques, we demonstrate how these images can contribute to enhanced semantic segmentation. Our results demonstrate that hyperspectral data enable more accurate object segmentation compared to conventional RGB data, ultimately demonstrating the potential of HSI data to improve semantic segmentation within urban settings.

This study reveals intriguing evidence of a complex internal rotation pattern within a less massive and less luminous star that has evolved into a giant. Typically, lower and intermediate mass stars retain their rapid rotation rates during their main sequence phase. However, once these stars expand into giants, we expect a faster core rotation rate compared to their outer layers. Contrary to these expectations, KIC 9267654's rotation speed is observed to be higher near its surface rather than at its core, which presents a challenge to angular momentum conservation principles. To validate our findings, we updated the constraints based on spectroscopic surface measurements, verified that the detected oscillation patterns align with the previously determined core and outer layer rotation rates, and confirmed that the star exhibits no significant chemical abnormalities. Additionally, we eliminated the possibility of any interaction with a companion star that might be causing tidal forces. Lastly, we examined possible explanations for this unusual internal rotation profile, including the possibility of the star ingesting a giant planet or experiencing enhanced angular momentum redistribution through the migration of helioseismic core convection phenomena.

In algorithmic complexity theory, the $LIN$ of-$k$ class represents algorithms with a worst-case time requirement of $O(k^n)$ for inputs of size $n$ and $k \leq n$. It's well established that $LIN$ of-$k$ is equivalent to $P$ and $NP$. However, there's no fixed upper bound for the number of non-uniform binary gates. The study aims to expand on this by introducing a new parameter, $p$, to establish a complexity class $LIN_p$ of-$k$ and demonstrate that $LIN_{16}$ of-$k$ contains the well-known traveling salesman problem, yet falls short of $NP$. Furthermore, it provably includes all conventional graph theory problems but can't solve the parity problem, thereby establishing an NP-completeness dichotomy. The proposed model uses a binary search process with $p$-ary steps to process inputs with $p$-ary edges within time $O(k^p)$, offering a new perspective on the design of algorithms.

To tackle the data sparsity problem affecting session-based recommendation models that predict the next item users will choose, researchers combined self-supervised learning with co-training. They proposed an enhanced framework by leveraging a session-based graph to create informative, not artificially sparse, data for these models. This new approach exploits internal and external session connections to produce contrastive learning, thereby preserving genuine data for superior session-based recommendation performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate the success of this innovative method in achieving state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmark datasets.

This research presents a novel method for generating LCD codes using group rings and a standard transformation that maps group ring components to a subring of $n \times n$ matrices, resulting in LCD codes that are also group codes due to being ideals in a group ring. Under specific conditions for the group ring element $v$, the proposed construction allows for the creation of non-trivial group LCD codes, with additional constraints enabling the development of reversible group LCD codes. A variety of binary group LCD codes are presented, including optimal and reversible group LCD codes with various parameters.

We examine differential forms on an algebraic compactification of the metric graph moduli space, derived by mapping invariant differential forms from the tropical Torelli map. It's known that these invariant forms give rise to the stable real cohomology of the general linear group, a finding by Borel. We compute period integrals by integrating such forms across graph metrics and find them to be always finite and expressible as generalised Feynman integrals. Our integrals have further application in identifying non-zero homology classes in the graph complex, providing novel perspectives on the cohomology structure and forging links between graph theory, motivic Galois groups and quantum field theory.

In various object categorization tasks, particularly in visually complex conditions, it has been demonstrated that recurrent neural networks (RNNs) can outperform feedforward models.  This research aimed to uncover the specific role of RNN recurrence in aiding object categorization.  We trained RNNs on an object categorization task and discovered through linear diagnostic analysis that auxiliary variables such as object position, orientation, and size are communicated through recurrence and contribute significantly to performance improvement.  This improvement is particularly observed in visually crowded scenarios.  We also found that auxiliary variables like background objects and clutters are frequently encoded in the recurrence of RNNs, and that object appearance is consistently maintained separate from these contextual elements.  These findings indicate that auxiliary variables are frequently integrated into RNN recurrence for an object categorization task, and that context information is frequently encoded in the recurrence of neural networks.

Despite numerous studies on non-Hermitian topology, the influence of correlations remains a significant unresolved issue. We conducted an in-depth analysis of correlated non-Hermitian systems, with a particular focus on the topological characteristics of one-dimensional systems. Our results reveal that correlations cause a significant reduction in the topological classification from $\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$, with local terms governing the geometric phase. We also discovered that embryonic higher topological classifications are thwarted by correlations, as seen in the case of the Fibonacci wave. To facilitate the interpretation of experimental outcomes, we established a correlation-induced topological difference measure. Consequently, one may anticipate the presence of correlation-induced topological transitions in systems like the one based on the Fibonacci sequence.

Recently, Golay complementary matrices have gained popularity due to their utility in omnidirectional precoding techniques. This research extends Golay complementary matrices to higher-dimensional spaces known as multi-dimensional Golay complementary arrays. By presenting a general method to break down these arrays into simpler forms, we show that they can be constructed using nested direct product recombinations of smaller Golay pairs. Additionally, we explore the existence of multidimensional GCA through a comprehensive examination of two-dimensional GCA, and propose a set of necessary conditions for their existence in higher dimensions. Computer simulations demonstrate that multi-dimensional GCA can provide significant improvements in system capacity compared to single-dimensional GCA.

Research on Higgs boson production is conducted, combining CMS data from 13 TeV LHC and previously collected data from 7 and 8 TeV LHC, totaling 104.6 fb^-1. The findings from four-lepton final state analysis provide joint constraints on Higgs boson width and its interaction with electroweak vector bosons. By applying matrix element techniques, production modes are separated and the Higgs boson width is constrained under the standard model's coupling assumptions to be less than 3.8 MeV, with the constraint relaxed to less than 5.3 MeV when considering deviations in Higgs boson couplings. The findings do not show significant deviations from the standard model predictions on the Higgs boson width.

Incorporating dimensionality reduction techniques, researchers address the complexities of analyzing numerous spectral bands within bi-temporal hyperspectral images. This study proposes a cutting-edge approach using a novel deep convolutional autoencoder that fuses features across hierarchical levels and receptive fields. By utilizing an unsupervised change detection technique, it overcomes the limitations of other label-dependent methods. By integrating various techniques to extract changes from the images, it significantly outperformed current state-of-the-art methods in unsupervised change detection across diverse datasets.

Consider the set $\mathcal{S}$ of squares and let $\mathcal{W}$ be a subset of natural numbers such that when you combine these two sets with addition, the result encompasses all natural numbers greater than or equal to some finite number $N_0$. Now, the $\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{S},\mathcal{W}}(n)$ denotes the count of all possible pairs of $s$ from $\mathcal{S}$ and $w$ from $\mathcal{W}$ whose sum is equal to $n$. Previous studies, such as those by Chen and Fang, have shown that the total count of these pairs minus the total natural numbers up to $N$ exceeds $N^{1/4}$ multiplied by the natural logarithm of $N$. In this research, we enhance their finding with a newly established lower limit, specifically $N^{3/7}$.

Quantum tunneling is an inherent process that lacks a direct analogy in classical physics.
In the realm of solid-state physics, it can give rise to undesirable current flow and unwanted interactions.
In this study, we examine wave tunneling in silicon, focusing on a silicon superlattice and a quantum dot separated by a barrier.
By employing the Heisenberg matrix formalism, we derive a single, unified equation that describes tunneling, wave tunneling, and electromagnetic interaction.
This approach enables the incorporation of Doppler broadening and Phosphorus donor orbits.
Wave tunneling is found to augment conventional tunneling by as much as $10^{-3}$ eV when influenced by Donor-Donor spin resonance.
Furthermore, we demonstrate that wave tunneling can enable the transfer of spin information between silicon islands and external magnetic fields, offering a promising mechanism for reading spin information stored in island charges.

Several disciplines have been influenced by optimization techniques in various real-world scenarios, hence their importance is being increasingly acknowledged by the community. As a result of this growing interest, researchers have been able to develop multiple open-source frameworks for optimization, ultimately contributing to innovation in both techniques and their practical applications. In the context of this study, we introduce a novel framework, known as LibOPT, for efficiently implementing and prototyping nature-inspired optimization algorithms. By integrating 15 established techniques and 112 benchmark functions, as well as supporting 11 novel hypercomplex-based approaches, our framework surpasses others in its domain, thus marking it as a groundbreaking innovation in optimization software development. Utilizing LibOPT under the C paradigm proves to be remarkably user-friendly and adaptable, as evidenced by the inclusion of clear source-code examples demonstrating the practical usage of benchmark functions.

Given an algebraic variety X that has a transitive action from the group Aut(X), the highest degree of transitivity of this action is called the transitivity degree. This degree is denoted by the maximum value of m for which Aut(X) acts transitively m times on X. In cases where Aut(X) is m-transitive for any positive value of m, we define the transitivity degree to be infinite. This study involves determining the transitivity degree for specific varieties, such as quasi-affine toric varieties, and homogeneous spaces, while exploring related open problems and conjectures.

In non-commutative space-time deformations, the definition of identical particles breaks down. These models are described by non-abelian space symmetries represented by a four-momentum group. Our focus is on the Fock representation, which allows us to explore the spectrum of these systems. However, due to the non-commutative nature, the standard number basis is ill-defined. To address this issue, we develop a consistent number basis for the Fock representation, which respects the properties of the non-commutative Poincaré group. As a concrete example, we apply our approach to a non-commutative scalar field representing a free real field. Our findings indicate that the mass spectrum differs from its commutative counterpart. Additionally, we generalize our methods to apply to the non-commutative deformation of the SU(N) group, represented by the Yang-Baxter disorder parameter.

We apply the two-photon absorption transient current technique to study
properties of wide bandgap semiconductors. We utilize this technique to
investigate charge transport in scCVD diamond by exciting its charge carriers
with a femtosecond laser. Due to its two-photon nature, the technique confines
charge carrier generation in 3-D around the laser focal point. This localized
charge injection enables us to map the semiconductor's conductivity with
high spatial resolution. We calculate the semiconductor's conductivity at
different points away from the focal point and plot a map of conductivity as a
function of distance. The conductivity at a point is influenced by factors such
as laser intensity, charge carrier mobility, and recombination rate. The conduct
of scCVD diamond shows an initial surge followed by a gradual decrease with
increasing distance from the focal point. The observed distance-dependent conduct
is attributed to carrier recombination. The capability of spatially resolving charge
transport properties in wide bandgap semiconductors could be extended to other
materials such as silicon carbide by adjusting the laser intensity to optimize
conductivity mapping.

Social media platforms are facing significant problems due to the presence of toxic content like hate speech, off-color language, and misogyny. These difficulties have caught the attention of the Natural Language Processing (NLP) community, driving innovative research in the field. Researchers have addressed these challenges by treating toxic content as a binary categorization problem, utilizing advanced methods such as recurrent neural networks and word embeddings. However, this approach has its limitations, and classification is often considered an underdeveloped field. To address these challenges, we propose a new technique by transforming toxic content into an ordinal categorization problem. Our approach utilizes the Ordered Neural Network model, enabling us to leverage various order constraints, our data shows that this method outperforms traditional binary categorization techniques, and we will discuss future research directions based on our findings.

This study centres around the solvability of a distinct class of fractional backward stochastic differential equations that take into account past influences within their generators, under Lipschitz condition it's demonstrated that the existence and uniqueness of such equations are assured. Furthermore, a key comparison theorem has been formulated.

We examine if controllers obtained using model-based Reinforcement Learning, which employs an environment model to find the optimal policy, remain robust and adaptable when dealing with slight environmental variations. Building upon the concept from PILCO, a method for probabilistic policy search, our research demonstrates that constraining the uncertainty in the Gaussian Process model's dynamics has a beneficial effect on policy updates and results in more resilient controllers. In addition, our findings highlight the practical advantages of this approach in a simulation-based evaluation.

Several key network communication challenges such as caching and computation caching pose crucial influence on wireless network design. This work focuses on the development of a novel centralized caching approach with integrated data caching and mobile computation caching capabilities. Our method achieves significant gains in both caching and computation caching fields. Specifically, this caching approach yields a reduction in communication load of no more than $VC/\left(k+1\right)$ in the caching sector, and a reduction in communication load of no more than $DC/\left(k+1\right)$ in the computation caching sector, where $V$, $C$, $D$, and $k$ represent the total amount of data, data bits, communication bits, and a positive integer without units. Furthermore, this caching approach satisfies a given probability of success known as the coverage probability and is applicable in various wireless communication scenarios including wireless caching and wireless computation caching.

We establish a formalization of the Scott model in univalent type theory, adopting a constructive and predicative framework. To capture the essence of non-terminating processes in PCF, we employ the lifting monad from topos theory, which has been adapted for univalent type theory by Escard\'o and Knapp. Our work confirms that using the lifting monad provides a viable way to handle partiality within univalent type theory, and we also demonstrate that a predicative and constructive Scott model is achievable. Notably, we avoid reliance on choice or quotient inductive-inductive types.

Hanzer and Muić's work on degenerate Eisenstein series cancellations has been built upon, 
extending their method and outcome to a specific set of Eisenstein series, 
specifically those formed from the combinations of two Speh representations 
$\Delta(\tau,m)|\cdot|^{s_1}\otimes\Delta(\tau,n)|\cdot|^{s_2}$ in $GL(m+n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ for self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation $\tau$.

Designing effective collision avoidance systems for mobile robots remains a key challenge, particularly when accounting for the robot's spatial structure.
In this paper, we develop a novel control approach that enables a mobile robotic arm safely avoid collisions by adjusting its movement.
Our method leverages Control Barrier Functions and Quadratic Programming to ensure smooth, obstacle-free navigation, allowing us to model the robot's avoidance behavior using a Quadratic Program that varies over time.
This approach relies on an approximate solution to the Linear Time-Varying Quadratic Programming Problem that is both efficient and applicable to real-time control.
To demonstrate its efficacy, we successfully tested our method on a mobile robotic arm navigating through a simulated environment.

Natural language processing, a crucial field of study, strives to comprehend text via digital analysis, despite the inherent imperfections arising from diverse forms of written and spoken language. This work delves into employing various graph-based methodologies for resolving the challenge of text summarization via a selective extraction technique. Two key indicators – sentence overlap and edit distance – are employed for gauging sentence similarity.

Researchers have suggested the application of quantum interferometry and information processing in Bose-Einstein condensates. However, the current understanding of BECs relies on complex descriptions, often through quantum field theory or nonlinear differential equations. These descriptions sometimes conflict with key principles in interferometry and information processing. Nevertheless, a possibility of compatibility remains, and we provide evidence supporting the use of quantum interferometry and information processing in BECs, thus validating the complex descriptions. Moreover, we identify potential obstructions, which could impede applications of quantum interferometry and information processing, and suggest remedies to overcome these limitations.

This paper aims to accomplish two distinct objectives. Firstly, it seeks to establish a unicity theorem for meromorphic mappings from a complete Kähler manifold to a complex projective space, under the constraint of limited intersection with hypersurfaces. Secondly, the paper aims to prove a unicity theorem for the case of nondegenerate meromorphic mappings that share a specified number of hyperplanes in a particular geometric configuration.

Polynomial system solving plays a crucial role in various applications to capture nonlinear geometric attributes. To obtain a solution set devoid of degeneration, which end-users seek to avoid, the nondegenerate locus of a polynomial system needs to be computed. The nondegenerate locus comprises points where the codimension of the solution set matches the number of equations in the system. Historically, the nondegenerate locus has been obtained using ideal-theoretic techniques like saturation ideals and equidimensional decompositions. We propose an algorithm leveraging signature-based features of Gröbner basis algorithms to directly calculate the Gröbner basis for the nondegenerate locus closure without initially solving the entire polynomial system through Gröbner basis computation.

Direct photons have been measured at $p_T<5$ GeV/$c$ for midrapidity and most central events in Cu$+$Cu collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}=200$ GeV. By calculating the $e^{+}e^{-}$ excess in the $e^{+}e^{-}$ mass distribution over hadronic contributions, we found that quasi-real direct virtual photons significantly contribute to the photon spectrum. In Cu$+$Cu collisions, photons show a clear increase above a binary-scaled $p$$+$$p$ fit, and their transverse momentum spectra follow a similar trend as Au$+$Au collisions, involving a similar number of participants. We have determined the inverse slopes of the photon excess spectra at $285\pm53$(stat)$\pm57$(syst) MeV/$c$ and $333\pm72$(stat)$\pm45$(syst) MeV/$c$ for Cu$+$Cu and Au$+$Au, respectively. Moreover, we found that the photon rapidity density in Cu$+$Cu is lower than Au$+$Au collisions by a factor of approximately $2$.

The Turan tetrahedron problem seeks to calculate the Turan density of the tetrahedron graph, K4^3, which represents a four-dimensional hypergraph with three edges that together contain every vertex. Our study focuses on determining an expression for the codegree squared sum of a given 3-uniform hypergraph. We find that this codegree squared sum equals a constant, denoted as v4, for all members of a specific class of hypergraphs. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the tetrahedron's codegree squared sum is maximal within a broader class of hypergraphs, in which every edge contains the vertex z. We also show that our obtained result provides an improved lower bound for the Turan tetrahedron problem, which more closely approximates the desired density than a prior conjecture due to Boston and Heinrich.

Achieving a seamless visual experience and optimal system performance when displaying line joins on vector maps requires an efficient anti-aliasing technique. However, the limitations of OpenGL API hinder optimal rendering results when approximating the anti-aliased effect through multiple triangles. In an attempt to rectify this issue, this study introduces a straightforward yet high-performance algorithm utilizing two triangles to replicate fan-shaped line joins via alpha operation. Our findings indicate this technique yields a genuine anti-aliasing effect while reducing memory consumption, raising frame rates, and preventing overlap rendering issues on both Windows and Android platforms. Moreover, our results show this technique outperforms existing anti-aliasing methods, producing a more accurate visual effect.

The multivariate interpolation operator is traditionally constructed using piecewise linear functions to approximate absolute differences between values. In this study, we develop a novel, transcendental interpolation function derived from the hyperbolic tangent, providing more precise approximations of functions that increase linearly with the distance. Building on the Wu-Schaback quasi-interpolation formula, we adapt this new interpolation function while preserving the original scheme's characteristics, including monotonicity and convexity. It has been mathematically proven that our adaptation converges at a rate of O(h^2), surpassing the original method's rate of O(h^(1-alpha)).

Pulsar halos are large-scale, high-energy emission structures, formed when energetic electrons and positrons break free from pulsar wind nebulae. As a novel category of gamma-ray emitters, pulsar halos serve as optimal probes for examining the diffusion of cosmic rays within the Galaxy's localized areas, as well as their escape from pulsar wind nebulae. Research on pulsar halos has brought to light that their associated diffusion coefficient is substantially lower than the overall average in the Galaxy, thus revealing an intriguing spatial variation in the rate of cosmic-ray propagation. To unravel these phenomena, researchers propose utilizing composite models that comprise two separate regions: an inner zone where cosmic rays are heavily confined and an outer zone where they exhibit near-universal diffusion. This model can successfully replicate the observed intensity profiles of pulsar halos, the time it takes for them to form, and their overall size. Nevertheless, the model still faces challenges in accounting for the observed spectral hardness of some pulsar halos.

Transportation systems are frequently hindered by unpredictable weather conditions.
